newsitem.title: UK: STERLING/MARK SLIPS BELOW 3.0 AFTER BOE NEWS.
newsitem.headline: STERLING/MARK SLIPS BELOW 3.0 AFTER BOE NEWS.

text.p: Sterling slid over half a pfennig to below 3.0 marks after the Bank of England raised rates by 1/4 point to 7.0 percent and said they have reached levels consistent with inflation targets.
At 1210 GMT sterling/mark stood at 2.9960/70 against 3.0120/30 ahead of the news and 3.0130 in late Europe on Wednesday. Cable slid to $1.5940/50 against $1.6010/15 ahead of the news.
Sterling's trade-weighted index at 104.1 at 1100 GMT against 103.9 on Wednesday.
Since May, the BoE has raised rates four times in order to help cool a booming economy. The UK now boasts one of the highest rates in Europe.
